what_changes: row 0, where EVERY cell is a recognized header word glued to its first data value (DATE01/05, DESCRIPTION..., AMOUNT$1,200.00), is split into a clean header row plus a correctly-populated first data row
what_does_not_change: every value keeps the SAME column index it already occupied (date stays column 0, description column 1, amount column 2); the already-clean second data row is untouched; no digit is invented or deleted
semantics_note: the date/digit_run delta is a CLASSIFICATION-BOUNDARY artifact of this census's own token extractor, not invented data: '01/05' glued directly onto 'DATE' has no word boundary before its first digit, so the extractor's date pattern (which requires one) reports it as two separate digit_run tokens ('01', '05') before the split; once split_fused_header_row relocates the SAME digits into their own <td>, the boundary exists and the extractor now reports the one date token '01/05'. No digit's value changed and no column changed -- only which category this census's own regex sorts it into
